questions.explanation: Lab results hold under lab conditions. Extending them everywhere overreaches the evidence.
questions.hint: Ask how far the lab conditions extend.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: The qualitative claim a number does not license
questions.learningObjective: Identify qualitative claim a number cannot support
questions.stem: A number shows a score improved. What qualitative claim does it not license?

answer.exemplar: It does not license a claim about why scores improved or about students' experiences of the change.

questions.explanation: A number measures magnitude, not cause or experience. Qualitative claims need different evidence.
questions.hint: Ask what the number cannot say.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: A rate used to support a claim about meaning
questions.learningObjective: Spot rate misused for meaning

stimulus.body: A study group cites a falling attendance rate to argue that students have lost motivation.

questions.stem: What is wrong with using the rate this way?

options.text: The rate proves motivation increased.
The rate is too small to matter.
The rate measures frequency, not motivation.
The rate should be reported as a count.

questions.explanation: An attendance rate counts events. It does not directly measure motivation or attitudes.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: The generalisation a description does not license
questions.learningObjective: Identify overgeneralization from description
questions.stem: A description of one team is used to claim all teams perform the same. What is the error?

options.text: It uses too many adjectives.
It understates the single team.
It credits the wrong team.
It generalizes from a single case.

questions.explanation: One team does not represent all. Generalizing from a single case overreaches the description.
questions.hint: Ask how many cases support the claim.

questions.subject: SEMINAR
questions.topic: Keeping a description at the level its warrant supports
questions.learningObjective: Keep description at warranted level
questions.stem: A description supports a modest claim, but the memo makes a strong one. What should the writer do?

options.text: Keep the strong claim to sound confident.
Lower the claim to match the description's warrant.
Add more description after the fact.
Remove the description entirely.
options.misconception: treats mismatch as reason to delete evidence

questions.explanation: The claim must not exceed its support. Lowering it keeps the argument honest.
questions.hint: Match claim strength to support.

questions.topic: What counts as support for a mechanism claim
questions.learningObjective: Identify proper support for mechanism
questions.stem: What counts as support for a claim about a mechanism?

answer.exemplar: Evidence that the proposed cause produces the effect under controlled conditions, not mere correlation or assertion.

questions.explanation: Mechanism claims need causal support. Correlation or assertion alone is insufficient.

stimulus.body: Two studies find opposite effects of the same tutoring program, but one used random assignment and the other did not.

options.text: The program works differently in every school.

options.text: The researchers disagreed on values.
options.misconception: confuses design difference with value dispute

options.text: The program is inherently contradictory.
